aspects.says: The channel inside an adaptor logs only with its own logger attribute, and a node without 00_logger.xml writes everything to the console unmasked.
basis: section:8.2 An Event Goes to Its Source's Logger, and a Channel Without One Writes Nothing

aspects.says: Hex dumps and packager traces are text no filter touches; a dump to share is made from a masked copy, which keeps the lengths and bitmap the host saw.
basis: section:8.4 Bytes and Packager Traces Are Text Too

aspects.says: ProtectedLogListener masks a copy of each ISOMsg that is itself a message of the event; strings and wrappers that dump messages themselves pass through in clear.
basis: section:8.3 The Filter Masks Messages, Never Text
section:8.3.1 Spot the Problem: The Exchange Record

aspects.says: QMUX writes no event for an answer nobody waits for; it counts it in rx_unhandled, which SystemMonitor prints with the other counters.
basis: section:8.6 A Late Answer Is Counted, Not Logged, by the MUX

aspects.says: A log event holds one piece of work, is created when the work starts and is written once in finally, so it keeps request, answer, duration and outcome together even when the work fails.
basis: section:8.1 A Log Event Holds One Piece of Work and Is Written When the Work Ends

aspects.says: RealmLogFilter compares the realm before the first slash exactly and stops the chain for every realm it doesn't name, Q2.system included.
basis: section:8.5 A Realm Filter Narrows the Log and Drops Everything It Doesn't Name

aspects.says: A bridge into SLF4J is a writer after the filter that keeps events whole; Q2's own SLF4J binding fails quietly on a current JDK without --add-opens.
basis: section:8.7 A Bridge to SLF4J Sits After the Filter and Keeps Each Event Whole

aspects.says: Logger.log delivers an event to its source's logger: an event without a source goes to Q2, and an event from a Log or channel that has no logger goes nowhere.
basis: section:8.2 An Event Goes to Its Source's Logger, and a Channel Without One Writes Nothing
